question: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the economic relations between the Centre and the States?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XII** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the financial matters and economic relations between the **Centre and the States**. It includes Articles **264 to 300A**.
 
• This part contains provisions for **distribution of revenue** between the Centre and the States, borrowing powers, and financial autonomy to states.
 
• Provisions under Part XII include **Article 268 to 269**, which specify taxes levied by the Centre but appropriated by the States. *Hence, Part XII is correct.*
 
• It also includes **Article 280**, which establishes the **Finance Commission** to recommend measures for the distribution of financial resources between the Centre and States.
 
• This Finance Commission plays a crucial role in maintaining fiscal balance between different levels of government. *Hence, this reinforces the correctness of Part XII.*
 
• Part XII also includes provisions for **grants-in-aid** to states under Article 275, ensuring adequate resources for states to carry out their responsibilities.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Part XII.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles under Part XII:**

 
 
• **Article 268:** Provides for duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.
 
• **Article 269:** Specifies taxes levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States.
 
• **Article 280:** Establishes the Finance Commission to recommend financial distribution between the Centre and States.
 
• **Article 275:** Provides for grants-in-aid to States from the Consolidated Fund of India.
 
 
 
• **Economic Relations:**
 
 
• Part XII plays a crucial role in defining the economic relationship between the **Union Government** and **State Governments**.
 
• It ensures that resources are distributed fairly and efficiently to maintain fiscal balance in the country.
 
• The **Finance Commission**, as per Article 280, reviews the financial position of states and recommends measures to ensure equitable distribution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Considerations:**

 
 
• Part XII also includes provisions for **Contingency Fund** and **Public Accounts of India** under Article 267.
 
• The division of taxes and grants-in-aid helps states to meet their financial requirements and manage their budgets effectively.
 
 
 
• **Finance Commission:**
 
 
• The **Finance Commission**, established under Article 280, advises the President on financial matters and suggests measures for equitable distribution of resources.
 
• It provides recommendations on issues such as sharing of taxes, allocation of funds, and financial grants.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The **14th Finance Commission** recommended increasing the states' share of central taxes from **32%** to **42%**.
 
• The creation of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** under the GST Act harmonized indirect taxation across the country, impacting Centre-State economic relations.
